claims.text: The as-synthesized nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a solid solution.
Multi-element mixing produces inherent lattice distortions in the PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst.
Intrinsic local lattice distortions modify the catalyst's d-band structure.
The modified d-band structure governs the binding energies of ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Depositing the nanoparticles on a substrate with a slightly larger lattice constant can impose tensile strain.
Surface tensile strain alters surface interatomic distances.
Surface tensile strain alters the local electronic structure and d-band center.
Induced tensile strain shifts the d-band center to lower energies.
The lower-energy d-band center weakens adsorption of CO poisoning intermediates.
The lower-energy d-band center weakens adsorption of strongly bound oxygenated intermediates.
Weaker intermediate binding facilitates faster intermediate turnover.
Weaker poisoning-intermediate binding prevents catalyst deactivation.
Faster intermediate turnover enhances ethanol-oxidation activity.
Reduced poisoning and deactivation enhance catalyst durability.
The tensile-strained catalyst will have a higher steady-state current density than the unstrained baseline.
The tensile-strained catalyst will deactivate more slowly than the unstrained baseline.
Tensile strain is expected to improve performance metrics by approximately 10–20%.
The unstrained catalyst has moderate durability because its intermediate binding energies are suboptimal.
The proposed mechanism should apply when induced tensile strain is no greater than approximately 2%.
The proposed mechanism should apply during ethanol oxidation at approximately 25–80 °C and typical ethanol-oxidation potentials.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says strain should be the only systematic variable, but compares substrate-supported strained particles with free-standing unstrained particles. Substrate contact, support chemistry, morphology, and transport therefore differ along with strain, making the claimed single-variable comparison internally incompatible with the proposed design.
